name: Callan JMB Inc.

profile.description: Callan JMB Inc. provides fulfillment, warehousing, cold-chain logistics, temperature monitoring, regulatory compliance and emergency-preparedness services, largely for life-sciences customers, and in 2026 launched an energy arm, Callan Power. In August 2026 Callan Power agreed to acquire 26 non-producing exploratory Williston Basin leases from Reger Oil for $10M of convertible preferred stock plus $2M cash, with Northern Oil and Gas founder Michael Reger to become its president; closing was due by October 30-31, 2026 and was not confirmed in research. A separate $12.5M Pfanenstiel acquisition was terminated. FY2025 revenue fell to $5.72M from $22.77M in FY2022, and the company faces Nasdaq equity and bid-price deficiencies with a hearing requested in October 2026.

innovation.label: WEAK
innovation.analysis: Track Record (1/3): The only notable strategic move is the 2026 push into Williston Basin oil and gas through Callan Power, including the pending Reger Oil lease acquisition, but it has produced no revenue and the core cold-chain business shrank from $22.77M revenue in FY2022 to $5.72M in FY2025 [3][4]. AI Deployment (0/2): No AI products or quantified AI savings were found. Market Share (0/2): At under $6M of revenue Callan JMB is a marginal participant in life-sciences logistics. Pipeline (0/2): The Reger leases are non-producing exploratory acreage with no development timeline, and the larger producing-asset deal with Pfanenstiel was terminated [5][6]. R&D (0/1): No R&D spending is reported [4].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Callan JMB presents itself as a service-disabled veteran-owned provider of cold-chain logistics and emergency-preparedness services for life sciences, a clear statement of what it does and for whom but not a distinctive purpose [3]. Community Impact (0/2): No quantified charitable or community programs were found. Employee Retention (0/2): A management resignation was disclosed in 2026 and no retention data is available [7]. Insider Buying (0/2): No insider purchases were found; CEO Wayne Williams already controls roughly 52.6% of voting power from before the IPO, while outside holders have been diluted by about 27% in a year through an equity line and a $5M at-the-market program [7].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 5 available growth metrics (7 weight units; forward P/E and PEG unavailable with no estimates). D/E of 314% is past the 300% floor (0.0), ROE of -300% (0.0, 2x weight) and a profit margin of -192% (0.0) reflect a FY2025 net loss of $7.97M on $5.72M revenue, revenue growth of -17.4% YoY scores only 0.09, and the FY2022-FY2025 revenue CAGR of -36.9% (derived from FMP annual statements, $22.77M to $5.72M) scores 0.0 at 2x weight [1][4]. Weighted sum 0.09/7 = 0.1, rounding to 0. The liquidity floor is narrowly cleared on average volume (2.73M shares at $0.42 is about $1.15M per day), though recent volume of 930K shares implies only about $390K per day [1].

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Callan JMB's revenue comes from physically handling temperature-sensitive biologics (warehousing, frozen shipping, emergency-preparedness stockpiles) and, prospectively, oil and gas leases, none of which AI can substitute [3][5]. Its monitoring and regulatory-compliance services are more exposed to software automation, which keeps it below the immune tier. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI revenue is reported.

infinite_game.summary: Through Sinek's lens Callan JMB is playing a survival game, not an infinite one: its core business has shrunk by three-quarters since 2022, it is fighting Nasdaq delisting, and its leap into exploratory oil leases looks driven by the need for a new story rather than a Just Cause. A controlling founder-CEO and continuous dilution of outside holders further point to finite thinking.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (0/3): The company's stated identity is a service description (cold-chain logistics and emergency preparedness), and the 2026 move into Williston Basin oil leases, unrelated to life-sciences logistics, shows no consistent cause guiding strategy [3][5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): A 2026 management resignation, a business that lost about 75% of its revenue in three years, and the strain of Nasdaq deficiency proceedings point to an unstable organization, and no evidence of an empowered culture was found [4][7].

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): No management commentary was found that references competitors as benchmarks for improvement; the company's communications focus on deal announcements rather than competitive learning [5][6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Callan JMB is attempting a dramatic shift by adding an energy segment and recruiting Michael Reger, founder of the $2.9B Northern Oil and Gas, to run it [5]. Sinek credits pivots driven by a cause, not desperation; this one coincides with collapsing core revenue and delisting risk, and the larger Pfanenstiel deal has already been terminated, so it earns only partial credit [6].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (0/2): Leadership has funded losses through an equity line priced at 95% of the lowest trading price and a $5M at-the-market program, diluting shareholders about 27% in a year, while the CEO retains majority voting control [7]. No example of sacrificing near-term results for long-term capability was found.

investment_thesis: The bull case is an option on a turnaround: if the Reger Oil acquisition closes, Callan Power gains 26 Williston Basin leases and Michael Reger, who founded Northern Oil and Gas, as its president, giving the company an experienced energy operator for only $2M cash plus preferred stock [5]. The underlying cold-chain business still serves life-sciences customers with temperature-controlled logistics and emergency-preparedness services that have real demand [3].
thesis_continued: The bear case is overwhelming: revenue has fallen from $22.77M (FY2022) to $5.72M (FY2025), FY2025 net loss was $7.97M, and Q1 2026 revenue was only about $1.11M [2][4]. The company has received Nasdaq notices for stockholders' equity below $2.5M and a bid price below $1.00, and requested a delisting hearing on October 14, 2026 [7]. Funding relies on an equity line priced at 95% of the lowest daily price and a $5M ATM, the exploratory leases are non-producing, the producing-asset deal was terminated, and the stock at $0.42 trades far below its 50-day average of $1.93 [1][6][7].
key_catalysts: Closing of the Reger Oil Williston Basin lease acquisition (deadline October 30-31, 2026) and Michael Reger's appointment as Callan Power president and director [5]
Outcome of the Nasdaq Hearings Panel requested October 14, 2026 on equity and bid-price deficiencies [7]
Any stabilization in cold-chain logistics revenue after falling 17% YoY [1]
key_risks: Nasdaq delisting for stockholders' equity below $2.5M and bid price below $1.00, which would also reset the Hexstone equity line price to 75% of the lowest trading price [7]
Continued dilution from the equity line and $5M at-the-market program after a roughly 27% increase in shares outstanding in a year [7]
Execution risk in a new, unrelated oil and gas segment built on non-producing exploratory leases, after the producing Pfanenstiel deal was terminated [5][6]
